points.description: States the central idea that an SVM finds a decision boundary/hyperplane with maximum margin separating the classes (in the simplest case, a linear classifier/learnable machine). Equivalent wording such as 'maximum-margin hyperplane' earns this point.
Identifies support vectors as the data points closest to the decision boundary and states that the margin is determined by these points.
Mentions kernels or the kernel trick as the way to separate non-linearly separable data.
Mentions that the SVM optimization problem is solved using quadratic programming (QP).

rubric.notes: Full marks require the maximum-margin decision boundary, support vectors, kernels for non-linear data, and quadratic programming. Award each point only when the student's answer contains the specific idea; vague statements such as 'classifies data' without margin or support vectors do not earn P1 or P2. No marks are given for unrelated classifier descriptions.
